title: Delhi Police personnel misbehaved with women protesters, Amit Shah must answer: Rahul Gandhi
author: PTI
content_html:
Senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday (October 3, 2026) demanded answers from Union Home Minister Amit Shah on allegations of misconduct with women by Delhi Police personnel during a protest at Jantar Mantar.

In an X post in Hindi, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha said that since Delhi Police comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Amit Shah must answer.

"A female journalist has accused a police officer of misconduct at Jantar Mantar. For hours, hundreds of journalists have been sitting there with just one demand: that an FIR be registered. Isn't that the police's basic duty? They haven't even done that," Mr. Gandhi said in his post in Hindi.

He said that on Saturday (October 3, 2026) alone, hundreds of people were taken into custody at Jantar Mantar.

"There are allegations of misconduct with women protesters. Cameras were snatched, journalists were dragged. And this isn't the first time — we've seen video evidence of police officers engaging in disgusting misconduct with women earlier," he said.

He alleged that women and students across Delhi, who are gripped by fear for their safety, are staging satyagraha, but the police responsible for protecting them are raising hands against them instead.

"And a government that fears registering even one woman's complaint — what exactly is it protecting? Delhi Police comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Amit Shah ji, where are you? You have to answer for this," Mr. Gandhi wrote.

Left-wing student organisation All India Students' Association (AISA) has also made a similar complaint.

"Women protesters, journalists and lawyers were manhandled by male police. Several women have complained of being groped by male police personnel," AISA said in a statement.

"A police force that claims to ensure justice to women cannot maintain basic protocols of crowd management. Male police officers openly abused women protesters and behaved in the most unprofessional way," it said.

title: Russia has agreed to take around 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year: Govt tells parliamentary panel
author: PTI
content_html:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Saturday (October 3, 2026) briefed a parliamentary consultative committee on India's "multifaceted" engagement with Russia, highlighting shared ambitions to expand bilateral trade, investment, and energy cooperation.

Chairing the meeting on India-Russia relations, Mr. Jaishankar also apprised members of New Delhi's stance on the Ukraine conflict and its recent diplomatic efforts to contribute toward a peaceful settlement.

The External Affairs Minister further informed the panel that Russia has agreed to take around 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, especially in the fields of construction and logistics, people familiar with the meeting said.

While discussing the trade and investment ties between the two countries, Mr. Jaishankar mentioned that there is a shared ambition to expand bilateral trade in a balanced manner, including through greater Indian exports to Russia in seven areas -- auto, pharma, food, marine products, engineering goods, chemicals and textiles, they said.

The External Affairs Minister, while highlighting India-Russia energy ties, said New Delhi's priority is to safeguard the interests of Indian consumers, they said.

Our approach is to maintain multiple sources of supply, he said, according to the people cited above.

In a social media post, Mr. Jaishankar said he highlighted various aspects of our multifaceted engagement including in trade, investments, energy, connectivity, culture and people-to-people domains.

The Minister said he also made a mention of India's "active support to dialogue and diplomacy to end the Ukraine conflict." The people cited above said India's recent efforts to contribute towards ending the Ukraine conflict and return of peace figured in the discussions.

Mr. Jaishankar also referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's meeting on August 31 with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek where he noted that "endless war must now give way to end of war".

Mr. Jaishankar travelled to Ukraine last month and also met with Foreign Ministers of Ukraine and Russia in New York few days ago on the margins of the UN General Assembly.

In his conversations, he noted that if India can be of any help in any manner to bring the war to an end, it was ready to do so, the people cited above said.

In this context, Mr. Putin's comments at Valdai Club in Moscow that PM Modi "has very good ideas for finding mutually acceptable solutions" to bring peace came up, they said.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha's recent remarks appreciating India's efforts were also noted at the parliamentary consultative committee meeting, they added.

Mr. Jaishankar also apprised the panel members about the government's efforts to secure release of the Indians serving in the Russian military.

He said that the government has engaged with Russian authorities, including at the highest levels, for early discharge of all such individuals, the people said.

Mr. Jaishankar told the members that so far around 140 Indian nationals have been discharged and the Indian side is in touch with Russian authorities for the whereabouts of 55 Indian nationals who are reportedly working for the the Russian Army, they said.

title: Centre considering new hydropower projects, including in J&K’s Sawalkot: Union Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal
author: Peerzada Ashiq
content_html:
With the 1960 Indus Water Treaty in abeyance after the Pahalgam attack in 2025, Union Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal on Saturday (October 3, 2026) said the Centre was considering new hydropower projects, including Sawalkot, in J&K.

“Discussions are ongoing regarding Sawalkote. We certainly intend to take up work on that project in the near future. These projects would not only meet the local demand, but would also meet the power demands of other parts of the country,” said Mr. Agarwal.

The statement assumes significance in the backdrop of Pakistan’s objections raised on the construction of Sawalkote dam project in July last year and February this year with India and had sought consultation. India suspended the IWT after the Pahalgam attack, which left 26 civilians dead, in Kashmir in 2025 and started working on several power projects.  

Built by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC), the Sawalkot hydroelectric project was coming up at the cost of ₹5,129 crores on the Chenab River in the Udhampur, Reasi, and Ramban districts and will generate 800 megawatts of electricity.

“Major hydropower projects including Ratle, Pakal Dul, Kiru and Kwar are progressing well (in J&K). The Centre is also looking at other projects in the future,” said Mr. Agarwal.

Praising the Union Territory administration, Mr. Agarwal said the projects under the Chenab Valley Power Projects (Private) Limited were receiving full support of the local government. “We are making good progress. We are getting the full support of the UT administration. We will also think about other new projects,” said Mr. Agarwal.

 On power deficit in J&K, Mr. Agarwal said around 14,500 MW of hydropower potential were identified in the UT and “the ongoing projects would help address the issue”.

 On the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, Agarwal said around 50 lakh people across the country had joined the programme so far, while J&K had achieved its first milestone of 100 MW.

 “J&K has achieved the first milestone of 100 megawatts. Once the momentum is there, the progress will definitely be fast,” he added.

Terming the rooftop solar programme in J&K “a good start”, Mr. Agarwal said, “We are now reaching the take-off stage. J&K has made a good start under PM Suryagar. Momentum has built and it will take off,” Agarwal said.

Earlier, Mr. Agarwal visited the Seva Setu Abhiyan Camp being organised under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana in Srinagar, where he inspected stalls and help desks and interacted with vendors providing services related to the scheme. 

The Seva Setu Abhiyan Camp is aimed at strengthening public outreach, facilitating citizen-centric service delivery and creating awareness among citizens about the benefits of rooftop solar under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, said an official.

title: Kharge writes to PM and HM
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah seeking their intervention in providing help for drought-affected Karnataka.

In his letter, Mr. Kharge said that Karnataka is staring at what could perhaps be the worst drought in 150 years and facing such a drought is impossible without adequate help from the Centre. He made specific requests, including focus on the State’s small and marginal farmers and the dry Hyderabad-Karnataka belt.

Mr. Kharge asked Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah to calculate input subsidy based on Karnataka’s updated Bhoomi land records rather than the outdated 2015-16 Agriculture Census, so that no genuinely eligible farmer is excluded. “Provide enhanced support for drinking water security and the cost of substitute power, particularly in view of historically low reservoir levels in the Cauvery and hydel catchments,” he further said.

title: Sagardighi MLA Bayron Biswas sustains burn injuries after fire erupts at West Bengal residence
author: Shrabana Chatterjee
content_html:
Murshidabad district’s Sagardighi constituency MLA Bayron Biswas suffered burn injuries after a fire broke out at his home in Samserganj on Saturday (October 3, 2026).

He was initially admitted to a local nursing home, and may be transferred to the Murshidabad Medical College and Hospital for better treatment. The family members have also said that he may be transferred to a hospital in Kolkata if the need arises. 

According to local sources, Mr Biswas is currently in a stable condition and is undergoing treatment and has sustained around 30% burns. Reportedly. His wife also sustained injuries in the fire while she was attempting to rescue him. 

Firefighters rushed to the spot and attempted to douse the fire. However, the cause of the fire has not yet been determined by the officials. The fire had broken out at around 11 a.m., according to the locals present in the area. 

Bishnupada Roy, Officer-in-Charge of the Dhuliyan Fire Station, stated on Saturday (October 3, 2026) afternoon, “Three fire tenders brought the blaze under control within an hour. The cause of the fire is not yet clear.” 

Mr Biswas is one of the MLAs in the Democratic Trinamool Congress who defected from the Mamata Banerjee faction after the 2026 Assembly elections and set up their own camp under Ritabrata Banerjee’s leadership. He had won from the Sagardighi seat on a Congress ticket in a 2023 bypoll, but later shifted to Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool. 

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari wished him a speedy recovery. “I have heard about it and will get details of the matter,” Mr Adhikari told reporters. 

“Deeply disturbed & pained with the news of my friend and colleague Bayron Biswas. Wishing for his speedy recovery. Get well soon Brother,” Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee reacted to the accident and wrote on social media. 

Senior Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury said that Mr Biswas was like his brother, even if they are in different political parties, and wished for his speedy recovery. 

“This needs to be investigated because the fire occurred against the backdrop of his colourful political career,” West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar said.

title: Panchayat elections in Rajasthan to be held in four phases from October 23
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Elections to the Panchayati Raj institutions in Rajasthan will be held in four phases, from October 23 to November 17, and the results for Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis will be announced on November 20. The State Election Commission released the poll schedule in Jaipur on Saturday (October 3, 2026), while stating that 4.03 crore voters would be eligible to exercise their franchise.

State Election Commissioner Rajeshwar Singh said at a press conference that the elections would be held for members of 41 Zila Parishads, 457 Panchayat Samitis and 14,403 village panchayats following delimitation and reorganisation of Panchayati Raj institutions.

Polling for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members will be held in four phases on October 23, October 29, November 4 and November 14. Elections for the posts of panch and sarpanch will be held on October 25, October 31, November 6 and November 16.

Mr. Singh said the counting of votes for panch and sarpanch would be taken up immediately after polling at the respective village panchayat headquarters. Elections for deputy sarpanch will be held on October 26, November 1, November 7 and November 17 for the respective phases.

As many as 45,384 polling stations will be set up across the State, while the model code of conduct came into force in the rural areas following the announcement of the election schedule. There will be 50% reservation for women in the Panchayati Raj institutions.

The number of electors in the villages has increased by 6.22% in comparison with the previous panchayat elections held in 2020-21. The elections for Zila Pramukh will be held on November 25 and Up-Zila Pramukh on November 26. Panchayat Samiti Pradhans will be elected on November 27 and Up-Pradhans on November 28.

Mr. Singh said the elections for the three-tier Panchayati Raj institutions were being held simultaneously, as the State Election Commission was fully committed to implementing the ‘One State, One Election’ concept.

“Elections for sarpanch and panch will be conducted using ballot papers, while electronic voting machines will be used for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members,” Mr. Singh said. The reorganisation of Panchayati Raj bodies has led to an increase in the number of Zila Parishads from 33 to 41 and Panchayat Samitis from 352 to 457.

title: Odisha Governor directs filling of teaching posts amid 70% vacancy in public universities
author: Satyasundar Barik
content_html:
With 70% teachers’ posts lying vacant in State-run universities across Odisha, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is also Chancellor of the Universities, on Saturday (October 3, 2026) directed to initiate the recruitment process for vacant teaching posts by the first week of November and complete it by the end of the month.

Speaking at a meeting on the ongoing recruitment of teaching faculty in State public universities at Lok Bhavan premises here, Mr. Kambhampati said, “filling vacant teaching posts was the next major challenge after the appointment of Vice-Chancellors in State universities.”

It is to be mentioned that Vice-Chancellors of 14 Universities were appointed on a single day after he assumed office as Governor.

“Merit should be the priority in the appointment of teaching faculty. Quality and merit cannot be compromised,” Mr. Kambhampati said, stressing the need to recruit the best available faculty.

“All eligible applicants be called for interviews instead of extensive shortlisting and scrutiny at the initial stage. Such a process would ensure that no eligible candidate felt excluded while giving interview panels a wider pool of candidates to choose from,” he said.

The Mohan Charan Majhi Government recently informed Odisha Legislative Assembly that as against 2,081 sanctioned posts, 1,441 positions were lying vacant in 17 public universities across the State. To deal with large-scale vacancies, as many as 825 guest faculties have been engaged.

Utkal University, one of the largest universities in Odisha, has about 57.78% (141) of total 244 sanctioned posts of Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professors vacant.

Ravenshaw University, oldest of all universities, has 267 sanctioned posts of which 167 posts were lying vacant. As per the information tabled in State Assembly, Madhusudan Law University, Odisha State Open University and Khalikote Unitary University are also yet to fill up vacant posts permanently. In Dharanidhar University, located in home constituency of Odisha CM, of the 128 sanctioned posts, 106 posts are empty. The university is managing academic activities with help of 68 guest faculties.

Mr. Kambhampati also sought details from universities pursuing accreditation and suggested a common tenure for vice-chancellors across public universities. “There are some universities where the vice-chancellor has a three-year tenure and some have four years. There should be a common tenure,” he said.

Utkal University, one of the largest universities in Odisha, has about 57.78% (141) of total 244 sanctioned posts of Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professors vacant.
Ravenshaw University, oldest of all universities, has 267 sanctioned posts of which 167 posts were lying vacant. As per the information tabled in State Assembly, Madhusudan Law University, Odisha State Open University and Khalikote Unitary University are also yet to fill up vacant posts permanently. In Dharanidhar University, located in home constituency of Odisha CM, of the 128 sanctioned posts, 106 posts are empty. The university is managing academic activities with help of 68 guest faculties.
Mr. Kambhampati also sought details from universities pursuing accreditation and suggested a common tenure for vice-chancellors across public universities. “There are some universities where the vice-chancellor has a three-year tenure and some have four years. There should be a common tenure,” he said.

title: SP changes candidates on two MLC seats, field BJP rebels
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) on Saturday (October 3, 2026) changed two of its candidates in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council polls, announcing the names of Akash Agarwal and Sanjayan Tripathi, both rebels from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), who had been demanding tickets from the ruling party. In Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers Constituency Mr. Tripathi has been named as the candidate in place of Kamlesh Yadav. In the Agra Teachers Constituency, the party has fielded Mr. Agarwal in place of Prakash Chandra Gupta. 

“The leaders joining today have been declared candidates with the consent of the two previously announced Samajwadi Party candidates, Prakash Chandra Gupta and Kamlesh Yadav. All Samajwadi Party workers and leaders will consider this election their own and fight it. Along with Dr. Akash Agarwal and Dr. Sanjayan Tripathi, Samajwadi Party will work diligently to ensure the victory of all the declared candidates in the graduate and teachers’ seats. Those who have made sacrifices today will always be respected, and when the time comes, they will be given a respectable place,” said the SP president Akhilesh Yadav, addressing a press conference in Lucknow. 

Mr. Yadav alleged the education system has collapsed under the BJP government with paper leaks ruined the lives of young aspirants. “Education and examination systems have collapsed under the BJP government. Uttar Pradesh has seen the highest number of paper leaks in ten years. The BJP government has ruined school education. There is discrimination in government jobs. Under the BJP government, gangs have formed in the education department, the BJP government has discriminated against and exploited teachers. The Samajwadi Party will include the demands of unfunded teachers, Shikshamitras, and the old pension scheme in its manifesto for 2027 Assembly elections,” said the SP president. 

“Both candidates were welcomed by our president Akhilesh Yadav, the decision was taken in consultation with earlier declared candidates. The decision will strengthen the fight for the cause of social justice. We are hopeful of winning all the seats going for polls in teachers and graduate seats,” said Udaiveer Singh, the SP spokesperson. 

Elections to five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council will be held on October 23, with counting on October 27.
